newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden will not join EMU at start - Dagens Nyheter.
newsitem.headline: Sweden will not join EMU at start - Dagens Nyheter.

text.p: The Swedish government will not be among EU members which join the EU's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) from its scheduled 1999 start, a respected Swedish daily said on Monday.
Dagens Nyheter said in a frontpage article headlined "The matter is already settled," that the door would stay open for a future Swedish membership of monetary policy.
"Take it as already decided. Sweden will not join EMU from its start in 1999," the daily said.

"Officially the government has not yet stated what it thinks about EMU, even if some ministers have expressed views. The Social Democratic Party's congress will take its decision in September and Prime Minister Goran Persson is expected to publish his opinion this spring.
"But there is, today, nothing to indicate that Sweden will belong to the core group in the EU which will begin to introduce the Euro in about a year and a half," said the paper.

The daily said the minority Social Democartic Party government's cooperation with the small Centre Party -- crucial to its survival -- could collapse if Sweden joined EMU because the Centre Party is firmly against membership.

There is also a strong current of opinion from the social democrats that could threaten Persson's position as party leader if he tried to force through membership, the newspaper said. -- Simon Haydon, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1004
